questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Maternal health, RCH & safe motherhood programmes
questions.stem: The minimum number of antenatal visits recommended under the Indian programme is:
options: Four, with the first in the first trimester
questions.concept: WHO now recommends eight contacts, but the Indian programme requires at least four, supplemented by Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan providing free specialist antenatal care on the ninth of every month.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Maternal health, RCH & safe motherhood programmes
questions.stem: Janani Suraksha Yojana was introduced primarily to:
options: Promote institutional delivery through conditional cash transfer
questions.concept: By addressing the financial barrier it substantially raised institutional delivery rates. Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram additionally entitles pregnant women to free delivery, drugs, diagnostics, diet and transport.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Maternal health, RCH & safe motherhood programmes
questions.stem: The maternal mortality ratio in India has declined chiefly due to:
options: Increased institutional delivery with skilled birth attendance and emergency obstetric care
questions.concept: Most maternal deaths occur around labour and the first 24 hours postpartum, so skilled attendance with functioning referral for emergency obstetric care addresses the period of greatest risk.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Maternal health, RCH & safe motherhood programmes
questions.stem: Iron and folic acid supplementation in pregnancy under the national programme provides:
options: Elemental iron 60 mg with folic acid 500 micrograms daily for at least 180 days
questions.concept: Supplementation begins after the first trimester and continues 180 days postpartum. Anaemia Mukt Bharat extends supplementation across all life stages with a 6x6x6 strategy.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Maternal health, RCH & safe motherhood programmes
questions.stem: The high-risk approach in antenatal care means:
options: Identifying and referring women with risk factors while continuing universal basic care
questions.concept: Since most complications occur in women with no identified risk factor, every pregnancy is treated as potentially at risk - which is why birth preparedness and skilled attendance are universal rather than selective.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Maternal health, RCH & safe motherhood programmes
questions.stem: Tetanus toxoid in pregnancy is given as:
options: Two doses one month apart, or a single booster if immunised within the last three years
questions.concept: Maternal antibodies cross the placenta protecting the newborn against neonatal tetanus, which together with clean delivery practices led to elimination of maternal and neonatal tetanus in India in 2015.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Maternal health, RCH & safe motherhood programmes
questions.stem: The couple protection rate refers to:
options: The percentage of eligible couples effectively protected by a contraceptive method
questions.concept: A rate of about 60% is needed to achieve net reproduction rate of one. Eligible couples are those where the wife is in the reproductive age group of 15 to 45 years.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Maternal health, RCH & safe motherhood programmes
questions.stem: The most effective reversible contraceptive method in the national programme is:
options: The intrauterine contraceptive device such as Cu-T 380A
questions.concept: Cu-T 380A provides protection for 10 years with a very low failure rate and no user compliance requirement, and is offered postpartum and post-abortion to maximise uptake.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Maternal health, RCH & safe motherhood programmes
questions.stem: Pearl index is used to measure:
options: Contraceptive failure rate per 100 woman-years of exposure
questions.concept: A lower index indicates greater efficacy. Method failure reflects the technique itself, while user failure reflects incorrect or inconsistent use - a distinction important in counselling.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Maternal health, RCH & safe motherhood programmes
questions.stem: Under the RCH programme, a woman is advised to space births by at least:
questions.concept: Short birth intervals increase risks of preterm birth, low birth weight, maternal anaemia and infant mortality. The recommendation is birth spacing of three years and first pregnancy delayed to at least two years after marriage.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Child health programmes, IMNCI & school health
questions.stem: The infant mortality rate is expressed as deaths under one year per:
questions.concept: IMR is the most sensitive single index of the health and socio-economic status of a community, being highly responsive to nutrition, sanitation, maternal education and health service quality.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Child health programmes, IMNCI & school health
questions.stem: The neonatal period contributes what proportion of infant deaths in India?
questions.concept: Because most infant deaths are neonatal and most of those in the first week, further reduction in IMR depends on newborn care - the rationale for Home Based Newborn Care by ASHAs and SNCUs.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Child health programmes, IMNCI & school health
questions.stem: The three main causes of under-five mortality in India are:
questions.concept: Undernutrition is an underlying contributor to more than half of these deaths rather than a direct cause, which is why nutrition interventions have such large effects on child mortality.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Child health programmes, IMNCI & school health
questions.stem: IMNCI differs from IMCI in that the Indian adaptation:
options: Includes the first week of life and prioritises the young infant
questions.concept: Since most deaths occur in the neonatal period, the Indian version allocates greater training time to young infants aged 0 to 2 months and incorporates home visits.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Child health programmes, IMNCI & school health
questions.stem: Under the Universal Immunisation Programme, measles-rubella vaccine is given at:
options: Nine to twelve months with a second dose at 16 to 24 months
questions.concept: Two doses are required because about 15% do not seroconvert to the first. Vitamin A is given with the second dose and continued six-monthly up to five years.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Child health programmes, IMNCI & school health
questions.stem: The vaccines given at birth in the national schedule are:
options: BCG, oral polio zero dose and hepatitis B birth dose
questions.concept: The hepatitis B birth dose must be given within 24 hours to prevent perinatal transmission, and OPV zero dose primes mucosal immunity before the primary series begins at 6 weeks.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Child health programmes, IMNCI & school health
questions.stem: Mission Indradhanush was launched to:
options: Increase full immunisation coverage by reaching unvaccinated and partially vaccinated children
questions.concept: It targets districts with low coverage in campaign mode, addressing the reality that dropout between first and later doses, rather than complete non-immunisation, is the main gap.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Child health programmes, IMNCI & school health
questions.stem: Under Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram, children are screened for the 4 Ds, which are:
options: Defects at birth, Deficiencies, Diseases and Developmental delays including disability
questions.concept: Screening covers children from birth to 18 years through facilities, anganwadis and schools, with referral to District Early Intervention Centres for confirmed conditions.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Child health programmes, IMNCI & school health
questions.stem: The most important component of school health services is:
options: Periodic medical examination with follow-up of detected conditions
questions.concept: Screening without treatment and follow-up achieves nothing, which is the commonest failure of school health programmes. Nutrition through the mid-day meal and a healthful school environment are equally important.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Child health programmes, IMNCI & school health
questions.stem: Anganwadi centres under the ICDS scheme provide all EXCEPT:
questions.concept: ICDS delivers six services - supplementary nutrition, immunisation, health check-up, referral, nutrition and health education, and preschool education - to children under six, pregnant and lactating women.
